clue.text: Making bad move, lose when winning

indicators.note: a bad move is a poor one, so these words are shaken into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A chess player blunders, yet manages to lose a game they were winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' tells you to rearrange MOVE and LOSE. 'winning' here means charming, the way a winning smile is, not coming out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone attractive and endearing, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Beaten for having given tongue

definitions.meaning: having run the tongue over something

explanation.surface: Thrashed for being cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: It means defeated soundly, and also passed the tongue over something.

clue.text: Face different directions in turn

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to veer is to turn
N and E are two different compass points, north and east

explanation.surface: Turning to look one way and another, in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin surface layer, a facing over cheaper material.

clue.text: Make notes about many a cast

indicators.note: around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: singing produces musical notes
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword 'many'

explanation.surface: A theatre company's actors each jot down notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a theatre company but is a verb: to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean throw or hurl.

clue.text: Came with the wrong knife

indicators.note: something done wrong is out of order, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone turned up carrying a blade they should not have.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a broad heavy blade used for clearing jungle, a type of large cutting tool.

clue.text: The thing is to protest

explanation.surface: The aim of the meeting is to make a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it names any item or article; as a verb it means voice disapproval.

clue.text: Support the boards behind the scenes

parts.note: to back is to support
the boards is an idiom for the theatre stage

explanation.surface: Theatre talk about propping up the set out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: It describes the area of a theatre out of the audience's view, and so anything hidden from public view.

clue.text: A break for everyone playing apart

definitions.text: A break for everyone playing apart

parts.words: A break for everyone playing apart
parts.note: read 'apart' as 'a part': a pause for all the actors, an interval in a theatre

explanation.surface: Everyone at the game stops for a rest, scattered around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing apart' hides 'playing a part', so it is acting, not a game.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the interval between acts of a play, a rest for the whole cast.

clue.text: Sure, try a new sort of bank

indicators.note: a new version means these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone is encouraged to try out a different bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A government finance department stores and manages public money, a kind of bank.

clue.text: Reassure but delude 5 in the Church

parts.note: to delude is to con or trick
V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A churchman reassures his flock while secretly fooling the fifth member.
explanation.walkthrough: The '5' looks like a cross-reference to 5-across but simply stands for the Roman numeral V.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone sure of something is to persuade them, a close synonym.

clue.text: Poor chesty grass-cutter!

indicators.note: poor here means in bad shape, so these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Sympathy for someone with a cough who mows the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a long curved blade used for mowing tall crops by hand.

clue.text: It's very comfortable with the arms raised

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read from bottom to top

parts.note: guns are arms, weapons

explanation.surface: An armchair with high armrests is cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' suggests limbs or armchair arms, but means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosy and warm, a close synonym.

clue.text: Ivy's always a sucker!

definitions.note: read as 'ivy is', so the definition is a describing word for the plant

parts.note: ever means always
someone green is naive, easily fooled like a sucker

explanation.surface: Somebody called Ivy keeps getting taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivy looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant: 'Ivy's' is 'ivy is', and ivy keeps its leaves all year.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a plant whose foliage stays on through winter, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Secures animals

explanation.surface: Someone fastens up the creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means closes or fastens tight; as a noun it names marine mammals with flippers.

clue.text: Keenness could well be an advantage

definitions.meaning: a lead over a rival, as in having the upper hand

explanation.surface: Being keen may well put you ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: It means sharpness, as in the edge of a blade, and also a lead over a rival.

clue.text: Weapon of German campanologist

parts.note: der is the German for 'the'
a campanologist rings church bells

explanation.surface: The arms carried by a German bell-ringer.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small pocket pistol, a kind of firearm.

clue.text: Greek seeking an industrious worker

parts.note: if you are after something you are seeking it

explanation.surface: A man from Athens is looking for a hard-working employee.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'graft' means hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a hard worker who puts in the effort is called this.

clue.text: View as a distinct possibility

explanation.surface: Seeing something as likely to happen.
explanation.definitionFit: It means an outlook or vista, and also a likely chance of something happening.

clue.text: Look into way out item on the menu

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an escape is a way out
lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: Checking the menu while hunting for an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin slice of boneless meat, often veal, fried and served as a dish.

clue.text: Book to keep for oneself

definitions.meaning: to hold back or set aside

explanation.surface: Booking something so nobody else can have it.
explanation.definitionFit: It means book in advance, as with a table, and also set aside or hold back for your own use.

clue.text: He's a trainee after sound equipment

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'He's a trainee after sound equipment' (4), gives EAR + L but has no definition of EARL; probably a word misread, and no source found
annotationWithheld.clue: He's a trainee after sound equipment

clue.text: Appropriate encounter

explanation.surface: A fitting meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old adjective it means fitting or proper; as a verb it means come across someone.

clue.text: Corresponds, writing about cheat being found out

indicators.note: around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: a cheat found out is exposed and shaken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Letters that reveal a fraudster has been caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being found out' rearranges CHEAT to ATCHE, and 'about' puts MS around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To correspond is to agree or be equal, synonyms of this verb.

clue.text: Measure a bone

definitions.meaning: a measurement from centre to edge of a circle
one of the two bones of the forearm

explanation.surface: Measuring a skeleton piece.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a measurement from centre to circumference, and also a forearm bone.

clue.text: Destitute man given some food in a refreshment room

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bar serves drinks and snacks
an egg is food

explanation.surface: A poor man is handed something to eat in a cafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A pauper who lives by asking for money is penniless.

clue.text: The cavalryman wanting a ship specially adapted

indicators.note: something adapted is reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse soldier needs a vessel converted for his use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially adapted' signals rearranging A SHIP; 'wanting' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a soldier of the Turkish or French-Algerian cavalry, so a mounted trooper.

clue.text: Share out the drink, giving an explanation

parts.note: to ration is to share out in fixed amounts
ale is a beer, a drink

explanation.surface: Someone justifies dividing up the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the reasoning behind something, the explanation for it.

clue.text: A light-weight wild cat

explanation.surface: A small wild cat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small unit of weight, and also the snow leopard.

clue.text: In general a dozen ought to be plenty

indicators.note: the answer sits within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Twelve of something should generally be sufficient.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a sufficient amount, as much as is needed.

clue.text: Consideration shown for fine royalty

parts.note: fine thread is thin
a king is royalty

explanation.surface: Respect shown towards a splendid monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Consideration is careful thought, a synonym.

clue.text: Those people holding gold as a speculation

indicators.note: one word grips the other, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: they means those people
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: People who have bought gold as a speculative investment.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a conjecture, an idea put forward without proof.

clue.text: Someone rating fools-so right!

parts.note: asses are fools
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge calls the competitors fools, and is happy to be right.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who values property or judges performance gives it a rating.
